summary: Tat'yana Katenina was a scholar in Indology and linguistics. She studied at Saint Petersburg State University from circa 1944 to 1949 and served there as a Docent in 1948.

Tatiana Oranskaia works in Indology and linguistics. She studied at Saint Petersburg State University and Kendriya Hindi Sansthan, and held positions at Saint Petersburg State University (1973–1998) and the University of Hamburg (1995–1996; 1998–2016).

Tatsugen Sato was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who earned a literature doctorate at Komazawa University. He served as an assistant professor (ca. 1968–1995) and professor (ca. 1978–1995) at Komazawa University, and also taught at Tokai and Ryukoku universities.

Tatsuo Hayashi studied at Kyoto University from circa 1919 to 1923, working in philosophy. He held academic posts at Toyo University, Hosei University, Meiji University, Tsuda University, and Rikkyo University.

Tatsuo Nishida was a scholar of linguistics, Sinology, and Tibetology who earned his doctorate from Kyoto University. He served at Kyoto University as professor and dean, at the National Center for Science Information Systems, Toyo Bunko, and the Japan Academy.

Working in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and philosophy, Tavivat Puntarigvivat studied under Luangpor Teean Jittasubho and at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa. He held posts at Kyoto University, Mahidol University, and the World Buddhist University.
Taw Sein Ko was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He completed his studies at the University of Rangoon, the Inner Temple (circa 1892–1893), and the Inns of Court (circa 1892–1893).

Tawni Tidwell is a Tibetologist who earned a Ph.D. from Emory University in 2017. She has held posts at the Austrian Academy of Sciences, the University of Vienna, and the University of Wisconsin-Madison.

Teizo Iyanaga was a historian and Japanologist who studied at the University of Tokyo. He held faculty posts at Nagoya University (circa 1949–1954), the University of Tokyo (circa 1954–1976), and Sophia University (circa 1976–1983).

Tej Ram Sharma is an Indologist and historian who completed a doctoral thesis at Banaras Hindu University around 1964–1968. He served on the faculty at Himachal Pradesh University from circa 1970 to 2001.
Tendzin Chökyi Gyatso studied under Lobsang Gyatso and the 14th Dalai Lama, and also taught Lobsang Gyatso.
Tenga Rinpoche was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied at Benchen Monastery, which he later founded in 1976. He served as Dorje Lopön at Rumtek Monastery from circa 1967 to 1984.

Tensei Kitabatake studied at Ryukoku University, later serving there as professor, dean, and president (1995–1999). A Buddhist studies scholar, he was also president of Gifu Shotoku Gakuen University (1999–2005) and taught at several other institutions.
Tenshin Tanouye was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under and succeeded Sogen Omori. He was the founder of Chozen-ji.

Tenzin Dorjee is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied under Geshe Sonam Rinchen, Geshe Lobsang Tsephel, and Geshe Dawa. He worked as a translator for the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives and at Pullahari Monastery.

Tenzin Namdak was a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Menri Monastery and under masters including Lobpön Tsultrim Gyaltsen and Shes rab bstan 'dzin rgyal mtshan. In 1986, he founded Triten Norbutse Monastery.

Tenzin Namgha earned a Ph.D. at Christ University. He has held positions at Christ University, The Tibet Fund, the Dalai Lama Institute for Higher Education, the Central Tibetan Administration, Daily Bread Food Bank, and York University.
Tenzin Norbu is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He has held academic posts at Columbia University and the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies.
Tenzin Tsenyi specializes in Tibetology and religious studies. She has studied and worked as an assistant and academic teacher at the University of Warsaw.

Tenzin Wangyal Rinpoche studied at Menri Monastery and under several traditional masters. He served as director at the Dialectic School of Menri, worked at the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives, Rice University, and founded the Ligmincha Institute.
